messages.content: What should a personal AI refuse to remember about me by default?

By default it should avoid retaining sensitive identifiers, health details, exact locations, financial account numbers, and secrets you paste by accident. Prefer ephemeral context and let you opt in to any long-term memory.
How should an assistant handle diary-like confessions?
Treat them as private. Don't rebroadcast them into other chats, logs, or examples. Offer support and practical next steps without sensationalizing or storing more than needed.
Can my personal agent email my coworkers about my mood?
Not without clear consent and a specific ask from you. Mood and health-adjacent details are sensitive; the agent should draft only what you approve and send nothing on its own.
Should a personal AI keep a permanent transcript of every conversation?
Prefer short retention or user-controlled history. Permanent full transcripts increase breach and subpoena risk. Let users delete history and export what they need.
Why run a personal assistant model on my own device?
Local inference keeps prompts and outputs off a provider's servers, which reduces logging, employee access, and breach exposure. You trade some capability for confidentiality.
When is a cloud chatbot a bad idea for private notes?
When notes include names of confidential sources, unpublished work, medical details, credentials, or anything you wouldn't put in a shared drive. Use a local or carefully controlled tool instead.
What still leaks even with a local model?
Screen sharing, cloud backups of the chat DB, browser sync, crash reports, and plugins that phone home. Lock down backups and disable unnecessary telemetry.
How do I talk to a local model without training it on my secrets?
Don't fine-tune on raw personal archives. Keep inference separate from training data. For chats, avoid pasting secrets; redact before any export used for training.
What is data minimization for a personal AI product?
Collect only what the feature needs, keep it only as long as needed, and avoid copying sensitive fields into logs, analytics, or third-party tools.
Should error logs include full user prompts?
No. Log codes, truncated hashes, or redacted snippets. Full prompts often contain names, secrets, and message content that don't belong in ops tooling.
How should an agent handle my calendar for scheduling?
Read the minimum fields required (busy/free or specific event you name). Don't upload the entire calendar to a third party or keep a mirror you didn't ask for.
Is it okay for support staff to browse my chat history?
Only under strict access control, with audit logs, and preferably with your consent for a ticket. Default should be no human browse of private chats.
A friend asked me to upload our group chat to an AI for a summary. Okay?
Not without the others' agreement. Group chats contain other people's words and personal details. Summarize only what everyone consents to share, or stick to your own notes.
Can I record a meeting and have an AI transcribe it without telling people?
In many places recording without notice is illegal or against policy. Tell participants, follow local law and workplace rules, and offer an opt-out when possible.
My kid's school photos are in a folder. Can the agent index them for search?
Be careful: children's images are sensitive. Prefer on-device indexing, avoid cloud upload, and follow parental/guardian rules and school policies.
Should an agent scrape my partner's messages to 'help our relationship'?
No. That violates their privacy and trust. The agent should refuse covert access to someone else's accounts or messages.
What is selective disclosure?
Sharing only the attributes needed for a purpose—for example proving you're over 18 without giving your full ID number. Prefer the minimum claim.
How do browser fingerprinting risks affect AI chat use?
Even without account login, unique device and network signals can link sessions. Use separate profiles for sensitive topics and avoid mixing identities in one browser profile.
Why redact names before pasting a document into a chatbot?
Names link stories to real people. Redaction lowers the chance that a log, bug report, or model memory exposes them.
What's a practical way to share a bug report without leaking PII?
Replace emails, phone numbers, and account IDs with placeholders, strip auth headers, and paste only the failing request shape.
I'm a journalist. What must a research agent never do with source contacts?
Never put source names, contact details, or identifying anecdotes into cloud logs, public tickets, or training exports. Keep source files local and encrypted; ask before any share.
How should an agent store interview notes about a confidential source?
Local encrypted storage, separate from general chat history if possible, short retention unless you explicitly archive, and no automatic sync to shared drives.
Can the agent email my editor a draft that still has a source's real name?
Only if you deliberately leave the name in and approve the send. Default to redacting identifying details in drafts headed outside your machine.
What is a safe default when I ask for 'background on a person'?
Stick to public sources and cite them. Avoid doxxing private contact info, and warn when material could identify a confidential source.
How should an AI treat a pasted meeting transcript?
As sensitive. Don't repeat private asides unnecessarily, don't post it elsewhere, and help you redact names before wider sharing.
Should transcripts be used to train our company model by default?
No. Training on transcripts needs a clear policy, legal basis, and stripping of personal data. Default opt-out for personal or HR-sensitive meetings.
Someone asks me to reconstruct what was said from a partial recording. Risks?
You may misattribute speech and expose private content. Prefer official transcripts with consent, and refuse covert reconstruction meant to spy on colleagues.
How do I ask an assistant to summarize a transcript safely?
State the audience, ask for redaction of names/PII you mark, and forbid uploading the file to a third-party API if it must stay local.
A 'support agent' DM'd me asking for my password to fix my account. Legit?
No. Real support won't ask for your password. Don't send it; report the account and change credentials if you already typed anything on a fake page.
How do I spot a fake login page the AI can help with?
Check the domain carefully, look for urgency and spelling tricks, and never paste passwords into chat for 'verification.' Use the official app or bookmark.
Someone claims they're from IT and needs my 2FA codes. What should I do?
Treat it as a scam. IT should not ask you to read back 2FA codes. Hang up, contact IT via a known channel, and don't approve unexpected prompts.
Can an assistant safely check if an email is phishing?
Yes at a high level: look for mismatched domains, urgency, unexpected attachments, and requests for credentials. Don't forward the full email with tokens to a random cloud tool.
Do open weights guarantee privacy?
No. Privacy depends on where inference runs and what gets logged. Open weights on a vendor's GPU can still expose prompts.
What is a good checklist before enabling a cloud plugin on a local assistant?
See what data it sends, whether chats are stored, retention, and whether you can disable it per conversation.
Should analytics include free-text search queries from my vault?
Avoid it. Search queries often contain names and secrets. Aggregate counts beat raw query logs.
How long should soft-deleted chats stick around?
As short as recovery needs—hours or days, not indefinite. Tell users the window.
Is scraping public social posts for a personal dossier okay?
Even public posts can be sensitive when aggregated. Prefer user-initiated lookups, clear purpose, and no secret dossiers on third parties.
Coworker pasted a screenshot of a private Slack thread into the bot. What should it do?
Warn that others didn't consent, avoid amplifying it, and suggest deleting sensitive content from history if the product allows.
What's wrong with pasting my full passport image for a 'visa tip'?
ID images are high-value PII. Describe the question without the image, or redact numbers and MRZ lines.
How can I use AI on medical paperwork more safely?
Prefer local tools, cover identifiers, and don't upload entire record sets to consumer chatbots.
Why separate work and personal assistant profiles?
Mixing them links your employer context to private life and raises retention and discovery risks.
What should the agent say if I accidentally type a source's phone number?
Warn you immediately, refuse to store or repeat it, and suggest deleting that turn from history and rotating the number if it may have synced.
Can the agent help me invent a cover story that misleads investigators about a source?
It can help with lawful safety planning and redaction, but it shouldn't coach deception of lawful investigations or create false evidence.
How do I brief an agent about a story without naming the source?
Use roles and non-identifying details ('a city official', 'a hospital nurse') and keep the identity map offline.
Should live meeting bots join by default?
No. Make joining explicit, announce presence, and store audio/transcripts under retention policy.
How to share a transcript excerpt with legal?
Export only the needed range, mark confidential, and confirm privilege rules with counsel.
What boundaries help for relationship advice chats?
Don't impersonate your partner, don't scrape their accounts, and keep advice from becoming covert surveillance.
Should the agent remind me of medications from chat?
Only if you explicitly set that up; meds are sensitive. Prefer dedicated health apps with proper controls.
Urgent email: 'click to avoid account closure' with a weird domain. Next step?
Don't click. Navigate manually to the real site or app, and report the email as phishing.
Is asking the bot to 'login as me' with my password ever okay?
Never. Don't paste passwords into chat. Use official auth flows and a password manager.
Can I fine-tune on my team's Slack export?
Only with policy approval and preferably anonymization. Many workspaces forbid personal export of others' messages.
What metadata does an AI SaaS usually see besides the prompt?
Account email, IP, device/browser, timestamps, and sometimes file names. That metadata can be identifying even if content is vague.
How should a personal agent handle passwords I paste by mistake?
Refuse to store or reuse them, tell you to treat them as compromised, and suggest changing them in a password manager—not in chat.
Can the agent keep my home address for deliveries?
Only if you save it deliberately in a vault-like field with your consent—not by scraping it out of casual chat.
What's a healthy default for 'remember this about me'?
Confirm what will be stored, show it back, and make deletion easy. Don't silently infer sensitive attributes.
Why disable chat history sync to the vendor cloud?
Synced history recreates a server-side copy, undoing much of the benefit of local inference.
Are screenshots of the local UI a privacy risk?
Yes if they include sidebars with names or prior prompts. Crop before sharing debug images.
Should I put API keys in the model system prompt?
No. Keys belong in a secret store or environment the tool runtime reads—not in model context that can be echoed.
Do we need full message bodies in product analytics?
Almost never. Prefer events like 'summarize_clicked' without content.
How to debug a failing agent tool without copying user PII?
Reproduce with synthetic fixtures; if you must use production, redact and restrict access.
Should CRM enrichment auto-pull a personal email into the agent?
Only with a clear user action and purpose. Silent enrichment surprises people and expands blast radius.
Recording a therapy session for AI notes?
Generally avoid unless the clinician and patient both consent under professional rules. Default refuse covert recording help.
Using a classmate's essay as 'style example' for rewriting mine?
Not without permission—it's their creative work and may contain personal stories.
Publishing an AI summary of a private dinner conversation?
Ask everyone featured. Private social contexts aren't fair game for broadcast.
What is purpose limitation in plain terms?
If you gave data for scheduling, don't reuse it for ads or unrelated profiling.
Why strip EXIF from photos before upload?
EXIF can hold GPS and device IDs that pinpoint places and routines.
Is a 'private mode' that still trains on chats private?
No. If chats train a shared model, treat them as contributing to a broader system—not private.
How should an agent label files that could identify a source?
Clear sensitivity tags, restricted folders, and no automatic cloud backup without your say.
Can it help me check if a paragraph is too identifying?
Yes—flag rare job titles, locations, and timelines that could fingerprint someone when combined.
What if a source asks me to delete all notes?
Help you find and delete local copies you control; explain limits if something was already published or legally retained.
Auto-deleting transcripts after 30 days—good idea?
Often yes for routine meetings. Keep longer only for projects that need it, with clear ownership.
Speaker labels wrong in a transcript—privacy angle?
Misattribution can harm people. Correct labels before sharing widely.
Should I paste a call transcript into a public GPT for 'action items'?
Prefer a local or enterprise tool under contract. Public consumer bots may retain or review content.
Fake 'DocuSign' link in email—how to verify?
Open the provider via a bookmark, not the email link. Hover carefully; watch for lookalike domains.
Boss on chat asking for gift cards—AI advice?
Classic scam pattern. Verify via a known phone number or in person; don't buy cards from chat requests.
Should I upload a suspicious attachment to the chatbot to 'scan' it?
Better use dedicated malware scanning. Uploading malware to a chat vendor can be unsafe and may leak content.
Boundaries for helping with job applications?
Help polish text you provide; don't scrape private employer systems or fabricate credentials.
Helping me draft a will?
Offer general structuring help and urge a qualified professional for legal validity—don't store unnecessary family details.
Does airplane mode plus local model equal perfect secrecy?
It helps against network exfil during the session, but disk encryption, backups, and shoulder surfing still matter.
Field-level encryption in the chat DB—worth it?
Yes for stored secrets and identifiers if you must retain them; still better not to store them.
Scraping a dating profile to 'analyze compatibility' without them knowing?
Refuse. That's invasive profiling of a third party.
Cross-device history—risk?
It widens the set of machines that can expose the corpus if one is lost or compromised.
Traveling with source materials on a laptop?
Full-disk encryption, strong login, minimize what's on the device, and consider leaving identifiable maps elsewhere.
AI meeting notes posted to a public channel by mistake—response?
Take them down, notify affected people, and review permissions; treat as a privacy incident if sensitive.
SIM-swap worries—what not to do in chat?
Don't share last-four SSN, account PINs, or one-time codes with anyone in chat.
Should the agent auto-share my location with contacts?
Only with explicit, time-bounded permission for a concrete purpose.
Using a remote GPU you rent for a 'local' model?
That's remote inference. Read the host's logging policy; prefer attested or trusted hosts if you must.
Copying prod chats into Slack for debugging?
Bad default. Use tickets with redaction and least-privilege access.
Parents asking AI to monitor a teen's messages?
Be careful of law and trust; encourage open conversation and lawful parental controls rather than covert message scraping help.
Aggregating 'anonymous' feedback that includes unique stories?
Small groups re-identify easily. Generalize anecdotes before publishing.
Agent proposing to text a source from my number automatically?
Require your approval for each outbound message; never improvise contact.
Closed captions saved forever on the meeting platform—concern?
Yes—captions are transcripts. Adjust retention in the platform settings.
QR code sticker over a parking meter—risk?
Could be a malicious redirect. Prefer official apps over random stickers.
Storing my therapy notes in the assistant?
High sensitivity. Prefer local encrypted notes and explicit retention limits.
Can browser JS on a 'local UI' exfiltrate prompts?
If the UI loads untrusted scripts, yes. Pin versions and avoid random extensions.
Do support macros need full account dumps?
No—pull only the fields for the issue.
Using a friend's voice sample to clone greetings?
Need their clear consent; non-consensual voice clones are harmful and often restricted.
Publishing benchmarks that include user prompts?
Sanitize thoroughly or use synthetic prompts only.
AI offering to find someone's home address for 'interview logistics'?
Refuse doxxing. Use official contact channels the source provides.
Highlight reel of a private workshop posted externally?
Get organizer and participant permission first.
'Verify your payroll' link after a breach news story?
Expect opportunistic phishing. Use HR's known portal, not email links.
Multi-user household on one assistant account?
Profiles and permissions matter—partners shouldn't see each other's private threads by accident.
Encrypting the model weights—does it protect prompts?
Weights encryption protects distribution theft more than live prompts; protect the chat store and memory too.
Webhook debug endpoints echoing full payloads?
Disable in production; they often leak tokens and PII.
Training a cute avatar on my child's photos for grandparents?
High sensitivity; keep on-device if at all, and don't upload kids' faces to random services.
